newsitem.title: USA: Hughes files $550 million lawsuit against Lockheed.
newsitem.headline: Hughes files $550 million lawsuit against Lockheed.

text.p: Hughes Space Communications International Inc. Tuesday said it filed a breach of contract lawsuit against defense firm Lockheed Martin Corp. seeking more than $550 million in damages.

According to the lawsuit, filed Monday in California Superior Court, Lockheed Martin and its corporate affiliates violated terms of a contract that called for Lockheed to provide satellite launch services to Hughes.

The lawsuit also seeks an injunction to prevent Lockheed from engaging in "unfair" or "deceptive" business practices and seeks to hold Lockheed liable for intentional interference with Hughes' contract for low-cost launch services.
A spokesman for Lockheed was not available to comment on the lawsuit.

According to the complaint, Hughes entered into a contract in 1994 with Lockheed-Krunichev-Energia International Inc. (LKE) -- a Russian joint venture 51 percent owned by Lockheed Martin -- that called for LKE to provide launch services using the powerful Proton rocket to Hughes.

Under the agreement, Hughes contracted to buy four firm launch services from LKE, one a year from 1997 to 2000, at a fixed price. In addition, LKE would provide Hughes with additional launches, based on availability.

However, in 1996, after demand for launch services had increased, Hughes said LKE turned down its requests for optional launches at fixed prices and instead offered to sell Hughes the additional launch services for higher prices than originally agreed.
Hughes said it is seeking at least $250 million in damages as a result of the breach of contract and another $300 million for interference from Lockheed.
Hughes Space is a unit of General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp.
